blocks.prompt: 9 (i) Let \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\). Find the domain and range of \(f(x)\).
blocks.explanation:
A fraction with \(x\) in the bottom, like Question 6.
We must find the allowed inputs and the outputs.
Plan: remove the zero of the bottom; solve \(y = f(x)\) for \(x\) to find the excluded output.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\).
To find: domain and range.
Method: Domain: \(x + 1 \ne 0\). Range: express \(x\) in terms of \(y\) and find the \(y\) that is not allowed.

Domain
\[x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -1\]
\[\text{Domain } f = \mathbb{R} - \{-1\}\]
Why: Division by zero is not defined.

Solve \(y = f(x)\) for \(x\)
\[y(x + 1) = 2x - 3\]
\[xy + y = 2x - 3\]
\[xy - 2x = -3 - y\]
\[x(y - 2) = -(y + 3)\]
\[x = \dfrac{y + 3}{2 - y}\]
Why: Clear the fraction, gather the \(x\)-terms, take \(x\) common, divide; multiplying top and bottom by \(-1\) tidies the signs.

The excluded output
\[2 - y = 0 \Rightarrow y = 2\]
\[\text{Range } f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\]
Why: Every \(y \ne 2\) gives a real \(x\) (never \(-1\), since \(x = -1\) would need \(y + 3 = y - 2\)).

Check that 2 never comes out
\[\dfrac{2x - 3}{x + 1} = 2\]
\[2x - 3 = 2x + 2 \Rightarrow -3 = 2\]
Why: A false statement: no input gives 2.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question writes \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\), but \(f(-1) = \frac{-5}{0}\) is not defined, so \(f\) cannot have all of \(\mathbb{R}\) as its domain (the book's own answer gives Domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{-1\}\)). It should read \(f: \mathbb{R} - \{-1\} \to \mathbb{R}\). All three parts are answered with this domain.

blocks.prompt: 9 (ii) Let \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\). Determine whether \(f(x)\) is onto.
blocks.explanation:
Onto means the range equals the whole co-domain.
The co-domain is \(\mathbb{R}\); the range was found in (i).
Plan: compare the range with the co-domain and point to a missing value.
steps:
Given: co-domain \(\mathbb{R}\), Range \(f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\) (from part (i)).
To find: whether \(f\) is onto.
Method: Onto \(\iff\) every element of the co-domain has a pre-image.

Compare
\[\text{Range } f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\} \ne \mathbb{R}\]
Why: The number 2 is in the co-domain, but part (i) showed no \(x\) gives \(f(x) = 2\).

Conclusion
Why: 2 has no pre-image, so \(f\) is not onto \(\mathbb{R}\). (It would be onto if the co-domain were \(\mathbb{R} - \{2\}\).)
blocks.final_answer: \(f\) is not onto \(\mathbb{R}\), because \(2 \in \mathbb{R}\) has no pre-image (Range \(f = \mathbb{R} - \{2\}\)).

blocks.prompt: 9 (iii) Let \(f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\). Prove that \(f(x)\) is one-to-one.
blocks.explanation:
A proof of one-to-one: equal outputs must force equal inputs.
Take two inputs from the domain (both \(\ne -1\)).
Plan: set \(f(x_1) = f(x_2)\), cross-multiply, expand, and reach \(x_1 = x_2\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \frac{2x - 3}{x + 1}\), \(x_1, x_2 \ne -1\).
To prove: \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\).
Method: Cross-multiplication is allowed because neither bottom is zero.

Start with equal outputs
\[\dfrac{2x_1 - 3}{x_1 + 1} = \dfrac{2x_2 - 3}{x_2 + 1}\]
\[(2x_1 - 3)(x_2 + 1) = (2x_2 - 3)(x_1 + 1)\]
Why: \(\frac{p}{q} = \frac{r}{s} \Rightarrow ps = rq\) when \(q, s \ne 0\).

Expand both sides
\[2x_1x_2 + 2x_1 - 3x_2 - 3\]
\[= 2x_1x_2 + 2x_2 - 3x_1 - 3\]
Why: Multiply each term of one bracket by each term of the other.

Cancel and collect
\[2x_1 - 3x_2 = 2x_2 - 3x_1\]
\[5x_1 = 5x_2\]
\[x_1 = x_2\]
Why: \(2x_1x_2\) and \(-3\) are on both sides; add \(3x_1 + 3x_2\) to both sides; divide by 5.

Conclusion and check
\[f(0) = -3,\quad f(1) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: Equal outputs gave equal inputs, so \(f\) is one-to-one. Sample inputs indeed give different outputs.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(f(x_1) = f(x_2) \Rightarrow x_1 = x_2\), so \(f\) is one-to-one.
